pageindex_flash.final_answer:
Here's how Disney expects its India business (Star India / Disney+ Hotstar) to contribute to segment operating income in fiscal 2025, per the guidance in the release:

**Fiscal 2025 expected contributions vs. prior year (fiscal 2024)**

| Segment | FY2025 contribution | FY2024 (prior year) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entertainment | $73 million income | $254 million income | Down $181 million (roughly -71%) |
| Sports | $9 million income | $636 million loss | Improvement of $645 million (swing from loss to income) |

**Key context behind these figures:**

- **Deconsolidation timing:** The Star India Transaction with Reliance Industries closed on November 14, 2024, forming an India joint venture (RIL 56%, Disney 37%, third party 7%). Fiscal 2025 includes only about one and a half months of Star India's consolidated operating results (through November 14), whereas fiscal 2024 included a full year. After the transaction, Disney recognizes its 37% share through "Equity in the income of investees" rather than segment operating income.
- **Sports swing:** The dramatic Sports improvement is largely a comparison effect — the prior year's $636 million loss was driven by the ICC Cricket World Cup costs, which do not recur in the consolidated results this year.
- **Equity method impact:** In Q1, Disney recorded a $33 million equity loss from the India JV, primarily due to purchase accounting; for the full year it expects an equity loss of roughly $300 million, also driven mainly by purchase accounting. This sits below segment operating income.

So in fiscal 2025, India becomes a much smaller direct contributor to Entertainment operating income, while its drag on Sports essentially disappears.

flat_bm25.final_answer: India business contributes $73M to Entertainment (vs. $254M prior year) and $9M to Sports (vs. a $636M loss prior year) in fiscal 2025.
